paper.title: Do Transitional Justice Museums Persuade Visitors? Evidence from a Field Experiment

claims.claim: Overall satisfaction with democracy increases by 0.14 (p = 0.03).
Trust in the church increases by 0.18 (p = 0.01).
Support for a military government decreases by 11% overall.
Belief that dwelling on the past prevents progress decreases by 0.32 (p = 0.03).
Support for victim compensation increases by 0.19 (p = 0.00 as printed).
Support for a public apology from the military increases by 0.18 (p = 0.09).
Support for pardoning perpetrators increases by 0.22 (p = 0.02).

findings.description: The main-text script failed before completion because the Figure 2 plot-label loop addressed rows 22:34 of a 24-row results table. The shipped outputs could not be fully generated as written.
findings.evidence: Unfixed run log reports replacement row-count error; changing only the label range to 22:24 allowed the complete script to exit 0 and generated all figures.

findings.description: The declared R packages were not installed in the initial environment.
findings.evidence: Initial runs stopped at vcovHC() because sandwich and related declared packages were absent. Installing the package set from the script requirements enabled execution.
findings.suggested_fix: Document/install the packages before running the scripts; record package versions.

limitations: The check covers the eight quantified main-results claims listed above; it does not adjudicate scientific correctness or perform robustness analyses.
Original code and datasets were not bundled. They remain available at the pinned Hugging Face snapshot linked in certificate.md and code/README.md.

Claim wording and printed precision were checked against the publicly accessible September 1, 2020 author manuscript associated with the DOI; page numbers in the claim list refer to that version. Publisher full-text access was unavailable in this check.
